key_insight: PAINT is a multilingual framework that standardizes how pain is identified and described across medical exam questions and real-world clinical text in English, Spanish, Portuguese, and Japanese.
clinical_relevance: By improving pain extraction across languages and documentation styles, PAINT can support more consistent symptom understanding for clinical NLP, research, and cross-language health data analysis.
method: Curated nine pain-focused dataset partitions across medical licensing exams and clinical texts.
Built a structured annotation schema for pain relevance, pain presence, location, descriptors, and demographics.
Used large language models with an ensemble strategy, then validated labels with clinicians across four languages.
evidence_signal: The ensemble achieved macro-F1 of 0.91-1.00 for pain relevance and pain presence, 92-100% accuracy for demographics, and inter-annotator κ of 0.82-1.00.
watch_item: Performance was validated on publicly licensed corpora and may not fully generalize to all specialties, languages, or local documentation practices.
paper_title: PAINT: A Framework for Multilingual Pain Representation from Medical Licensing Exams to Real-World Clinical Texts
